neighbours.label: 'return' / 'back' meaning a return TO a previous state or place (returns to, falls back to), as opposed to coming back FROM a trip (the - pole)
fire: Once the medicine wears off, his blood pressure returns to normal.
After the strike, the workers went back to their old schedule.
The excited atom quickly falls back to its lowest energy level.
Many hope the country will return to peace after the elections.
When the rain stopped, the river slowly went back to its usual level.
After a short pause, the ball bounces and returns to the player's hand.
Most patients return to their previous weight within a year.
Prices are expected to drop back to last year's level by spring.
quiet: He recently returned from a long business trip to Brazil.
After the strike, the workers moved to a new schedule.
The excited atom quickly gives off light of a single colour.
Many hope the country will move to elections next spring.
When the rain stopped, the river slowly rose above its usual level.
After a short pause, the ball bounces and rolls under the table.
She just got back from a week in Korea with her sister.
Prices are expected to rise above last year's level by spring.

notes: Card: ' back' x15, ' return' x8 of top 32, followed by 'to <state>' (return to democracy, falls back to its ground state); the - pole is 'returned from <trip>', and the + output direction suppresses ' from'. Near misses use 'returned/back from' travel and non-return verbs.
